UDP (WireGuard and WARP, games, QUIC). Where the node\'s link says udp=1 (raycontrol from v0.30.0): as HTTP/3 datagrams over QUIC once a check on the network has passed; before that, and where QUIC does not pass, in a TCP stream of the tunnel (sing-box\'s UDP-over-TCP v2). Off, naive carries TCP only.

Use N concurrent tunnel connections to be more robust under bad network conditions. More connections make the tunneling easier to detect and less secure. naive profiles check certificates inside Chromium, by its rules, and are held to the list chosen here besides. Under Chrome\'s list: a root must be both in Chromium\'s own list and in the app\'s list of Chrome\'s roots, which leaves out the certificate authorities marked China (nine roots Chromium has are not in it). Under Mozilla\'s list: both in Chromium\'s list and in Mozilla\'s. Under the system\'s store: Chromium\'s list and this phone\'s roots, those over HTTP/2 only unless the switch below is on. A profile with its own key pins or its own certificate follows those instead; an imported ca.pem does not reach naive.

Base64 or hex, one per line. Replaces the CA check, so a self-signed certificate works without "allow insecure". A naive profile checks the pin and the CA both, and needs a server name (SNI) for it. Get it with: openssl x509 -in cert.pem -pubkey -noout | openssl pkey -pubin -outform der | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | base64

Send the second QUIC Initial first

Hysteria2, TUIC, and naive over QUIC (its HTTP/3 datagrams too). A box that judges the flow by its first packets sees the fakes, or a ClientHello without the server name: a post-quantum ClientHello takes two Initial packets, and the second one goes first. A raycontrol node drops the fakes; for another server give them a TTL that ends before it (fewer hops than the server). Reordering does nothing under Hysteria2 obfs (no visible Initial there); with naive it costs some speed (each packet takes one more copy), and the fakes make its start unlike a browser\'s.

Before connecting, sends TCP SYNs or UDP datagrams to these ports of the server, in order. UDP steps may carry a hex payload: 1234/udp:68656c6c6f. SPA: 62201/spa:KEY sends one signed datagram that cannot be replayed (KEY = 64 hex digits, as on the server); 62201/spa1m:KEY hides its time too, if the server reads SPA v1m (v1 sends the time in clear, which DPI can match). Knocks again after a network change and when a connection fails. If a UDP session (WireGuard, Hysteria2, TUIC) gets no reply for the silence timeout after sending, knocks once more and logs whether the server answers again. Leave the sequence empty to disable.
Re-knock if a UDP session gets no reply, seconds (0 = off)
